eli5.text: If you're using the free version of the assistant with the 'no review' option turned on, the code-review step has been removed entirely. Previously, even in no-review mode, the assistant would still spawn a separate reviewer agent for free-tier users; now it skips that reviewer and runs only the type-checking and test bashers in parallel. This means a faster, leaner run when you've explicitly disabled reviews, and it's live today.

ai.title: Intersperse inline ads within assistant responses instead of anchoring
ai.summary: Replaced the legacy single-ad-per-anchor placement model (`placedAds`, `InlineAdBanner`, `computeInlineAdAdditions`, `isCompletedAnswer`) with a per-prompt batch model: `useGravityAd` now auctions `ADS_PER_PROMPT` ads per genuine user prompt and computes `responseAds` keyed by assistant message id via `computeResponseAds`. `blocks-renderer.tsx` reads `responseAds` from `useMessageBlockStore` and intersperses `AdCard` nodes between rendered response nodes using `responseAdNodePositions`, which places an ad after every `RESPONSE_AD_NODE_STEP` node only when a following node exists, so short responses show fewer ads. `chat.tsx` passes `responseAds` into the message-block context and routes ad click/impression callbacks through `handleAdClick`/`handleAdImpression`, while the rotating above-input `SingleAdBanner` now auctions separately via `slotPlacementId` for reporting continuity.
ai.evidence: Commit 0a6df576 adds `cli/src/utils/response-ad-positions.ts` (defining `RESPONSE_AD_NODE_STEP` and `responseAdNodePositions`) and replaces the prior `placedAds`/`InlineAdBanner`/`computeInlineAdAdditions`/`isCompletedAnswer`/`AdPacing`/`inlineAdAnchorIds` exports in `use-gravity-ad.ts`, now exposing `responseAds` keyed by assistant message id computed via `computeResponseAds` from messages and `PromptAdBatch[]`; `blocks-renderer.tsx` reads `state.context.responseAds[messageId]` from `useMessageBlockStore` and intersperses `AdCard` nodes between render via `responseAdNodePositions`

facts: The payload rides as a numeric byte array, which keeps the script free of double quotes and string interpolation (the no-`"` invariant the quoting below relies on) and avoids any Console.Out encoding translation, so the reset payload arrives byte-exact.

entries.title: CLI update: terminal-watchdog

ai.title: Windows terminal watchdog drops EncodedCommand
ai.summary: The Windows terminal watchdog now invokes powershell.exe with plain `-Command` text instead of `-EncodedCommand` base64 payloads. This change prevents the CLI from triggering EDR/AV heuristics that flag encoded PowerShell spawns while keeping command lines auditable in process listings. The reset payload is now serialized as a numeric byte array to maintain the no-double-quote invariant required for safe quoting. Additionally, `stopTerminalWatchdog` now nullifies the disarm path if the child process fails to spawn, preventing orphaned disarm files.

eli5.text: When the command-line tool starts a hidden background process that resets your terminal window on Windows, it no longer hides its instructions inside a secret scrambled code that some security scanners flag as suspicious. Instead it now sends those instructions as readable text, so if you ever peeked at the running process you'd see plain words instead of a long string of random-looking characters. As part of that, the tool also makes sure it won't accidentally leave behind a stale cleanup file when the background process fails to start. This is live today for anyone using the command-line tool on Windows.

ai.title: Pass apiKey to token count API in run-agent-step
ai.summary: Explicitly pass params.apiKey to callTokenCountAPI in packages/agent-runtime/src/run-agent-step.ts. Fixes failure of web API context token count checks for interactive CLI users lacking CODEBUFF_API_KEY in environment, which previously forced fallback to less accurate local estimates. Scope limited to agent runtime step loop.

eli5.text: When you run the assistant interactively from the command line, it now correctly counts how many tokens your conversation is using instead of falling back to a rough guess. It does this by explicitly handing over your personal API key to the token-counting step, which was previously left blank and causing that step to fail every time. The upshot: you get a more accurate read on how close you are to the conversation limit instead of the system silently switching to an estimate.
